description: Conditionals and loops for test logic.

questions.question: How does an if / else if / else chain decide which branch runs?
What is the ternary operator and when should you use it?
questions.answer:
The ternary operator condition ? a : b evaluates to a when the condition is truthy and b otherwise. Use it for short assignments, but prefer if/else when the logic is longer than one line.

code:
const expected = page.isVisible() ? 'visible' : 'hidden';

real example:
Building per-browser config with const headed = process.env.CI ? false : true keeps one-liner branching readable inside Playwright projects.

questions.question: What happens when a switch case block has no break statement?
How does the for loop with let differ from one with var in terms of iteration variables?
What is the purpose of break and continue in loops?
What is the difference between for...of and for...in?
questions.answer:
for...of iterates over values of arrays, strings, and other iterables. for...in iterates over enumerable property keys of an object, and it is not meant for array iteration.

code:
const arr = ['a', 'b'];
for (const v of arr) console.log(v);            // a b
const obj = { a: 1, b: 2 };
for (const k in obj) console.log(k, obj[k]);    // a 1 b 2

real example:
Use for...of to walk page locator results from page.locator('.row').all() so each element is handled by value, never by accidental property key.

questions.question: How many times does a do...while loop run at minimum?
Why is checking if (count) risky when count could be 0?
What does a while loop do when its condition never becomes falsy?
How do you loop over both keys and values of an object?
What is short-circuit evaluation in conditionals?
What is the purpose of labeled statements with break?
How do you iterate over the characters of a string?
questions.answer:
A for...of loop visits each character by value, including emoji, while indexing by position can split surrogate pairs.

code:
for (const ch of 'abc') {
  console.log(ch);  // a b c
}

real example:
Validating that every character of an order code is a digit uses a for...of loop over the code string before asserting against the alphanumeric rule.
